notes: Assertions: with_skill 28/28, without_skill 25/28. All three failures are knowledge the base model cannot have: the upstream archive and version pin (eval-2), and two SSE streaming details (eval-3).
16 of the 28 assertions pass in BOTH configurations. Evals 0, 1 and 4 are entirely non-discriminating by score, so most of this assertion set is measuring the base model, not the skill.

The score understates eval-4. Both runs pass 6/6, but only the with_skill run found that Labs already retrieves description and relevanceScore and discards them before curation, a two-line change. That is the most valuable output of the benchmark and no assertion rewards it.

The baseline beat the skill once. Eval-3 without_skill sidesteps the late-metadata problem by minting its own chatId client-side, so it never parses metadata to continue a conversation. references/api.md says to keep chatId but never says you can supply it.
Baselines are contamination-free: zero mentions of archive, sunset, 3.1.3 or Workday across all five without_skill runs, so the eval-2 delta is genuine rather than leakage.
Cost is roughly flat. The skill's price is context, not latency or tokens.
